name: Corruption Invariant Person Re-identification Benchmarks
description: When deploying person re-identification (ReID) model in safety-critical applications, it is pivotal to understanding the robustness of the model against a diverse array of image corruptions. However, current evaluations of person ReID only consider the performance on clean datasets and ignore images in various corrupted scenarios. In this work, we comprehensively establish six ReID benchmarks for learning corruption invariant representation. In the field of ReID, we are the first to conduct an exhaustive study on corruption invariant learning in single- and cross-modality datasets, including Market-1501, CUHK03, MSMT17, RegDB, SYSU-MM01. evaluation_method: mAP and CMC/rank-k retrieval accuracy under corruption settings
reputation: A specialized robustness benchmark in the person re-identification community, mainly used in research on corruption-invariant representation learning rather than broad leaderboard competition.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark focused on corrupted ReID images; results depend heavily on corruption type and dataset/modality, and reported scores are not directly comparable across the six benchmark settings.
